nodes.title: OIDC Discovery Issuer
nodes.summary: Trust only configured OIDC providers and exact HTTPS discovery endpoints, with byte-for-byte issuer matching. This prevents issuer mix-up, malicious-provider redirects, and SSRF through provider configuration.
nodes.probe: Parse provider configuration and discovery responses; assert exact issuer equality, HTTPS for every endpoint, approved hosts, and no endpoint derived from request parameters. Send a request with a malicious provider URL and assert it is rejected before any outbound fetch.

nodes.title: Authorization Code PKCE
nodes.summary: Use one-time authorization code flow with an S256 PKCE verifier for public and browser clients, while disabling implicit and password grants. This prevents code interception and front-channel token or password exposure.
nodes.probe: Capture an authorization request in an integration test and assert response_type=code, a unique code_challenge, and code_challenge_method=S256. Assert the callback URL contains no access_token, and reject configurations enabling implicit or password grants.

nodes.title: State Nonce Redirect Binding
nodes.summary: Bind high-entropy, single-use state and nonce values to each login transaction and allow only exact pre-registered redirects. This prevents login CSRF, response swapping, replay, and open-redirect leakage.
nodes.probe: Run two concurrent logins, swap their state, nonce, and redirect URI in callbacks, and assert each altered callback returns 400/401 with no session. Parse redirect configuration and assert only exact allowlist matches are accepted.

nodes.title: Token Validation
nodes.summary: Accept JWTs only after trusted-JWKS signature verification with an explicit algorithm allowlist and required identity and temporal claims. This blocks forged, confused, expired, cross-issuer, and not-yet-valid tokens.
nodes.probe: Feed the verifier fixtures with invalid signatures, alg=none, unapproved algorithms, wrong iss/aud/azp, expired exp, and future nbf; assert every fixture returns 401. Exercise unknown kid and JWKS outage cases and assert no token is accepted.

nodes.title: Access Token Audience
nodes.summary: Require each API to accept only correctly issued access tokens with its exact audience and required scopes, never OIDC ID tokens. This prevents token substitution across clients and services.
nodes.probe: Send a correctly signed ID token and a correctly signed access token with the wrong aud to every protected API and assert 401/403. Assert success only for a correctly audienced access token carrying the required scope.

nodes.title: Browser Token Storage
nodes.summary: Keep browser bearer credentials in a server-side BFF session or short-lived memory, never persistent Web Storage, URLs, DOM content, or JavaScript-readable cookies. This limits theft through XSS, extensions, history, referrers, and shared workstations.
nodes.probe: Scan source and built bundles for localStorage/sessionStorage assignments containing token names. Run a browser login test and assert no bearer token exists in storage, DOM, URL, or a non-HttpOnly cookie.

nodes.title: Native Token Storage
nodes.summary: Store mobile refresh tokens in the platform keystore or keychain and use claimed HTTPS or loopback redirects with unambiguous app identity. This prevents other applications, backups, logs, and crash artifacts from stealing credentials.
nodes.probe: Inspect the mobile package and end-to-end login flow for Keystore/Keychain use, plaintext preferences/database writes, logs, and backup exclusions. Complete login and assert the redirect is claimed and uniquely bound to the app.

nodes.title: Refresh Token Rotation
nodes.summary: Rotate refresh tokens on every redemption, detect reuse and revoke the token family, and revoke sessions on logout, reset, or compromise. This prevents copied refresh tokens from creating an indefinitely usable session.
nodes.probe: Redeem one refresh token twice, including concurrent requests, and assert the second and all descendants fail with invalid_grant. Execute logout and password-reset flows and assert subsequent access-token requests return 401.

nodes.title: Session Cookie Hardening
nodes.summary: Issue high-entropy opaque session identifiers with Secure, HttpOnly, appropriate SameSite, narrow scope, and preferably the __Host- prefix. This reduces theft, injection, fixation, and cross-site sending.
nodes.probe: Run curl -sS -D - against login and session-refresh endpoints, parse every session Set-Cookie, and assert the required flags, no broad Domain, and at least 128 bits of unpredictability across samples.

nodes.title: Session Lifecycle
nodes.summary: Rotate session identifiers at authentication and privilege changes, enforce idle and absolute lifetimes, and invalidate server-side state on logout or disablement. This prevents fixation and abandoned or disabled sessions remaining valid.
nodes.probe: Compare pre-auth and post-auth identifiers, perform a role change, wait through configured idle and absolute limits, then use old and expired sessions after logout or disablement; assert each receives 401.

nodes.title: CSRF State Changes
nodes.summary: Require framework CSRF tokens and trusted Origin or Referer validation on every state-changing cookie-authenticated request, with SameSite as defense in depth. This blocks attacker-controlled transfers, changes, and destructive actions.
nodes.probe: For each state-changing route, send an untrusted Origin with no token and assert 403 plus no state change. Repeat with a valid token and trusted origin and assert success; test missing/null origins according to documented policy.

nodes.title: Deny by Default Authorization
nodes.summary: Require every route, RPC, job, and tool action to authenticate and pass an explicit server-side policy, denying unknown actions and policy errors. This prevents newly added or unavailable policy paths from failing open.
nodes.probe: Enumerate the route/action registry, call each without authentication, invoke unknown actions, and inject policy-service errors; assert 401/403, no side effect, and CI failure for any unbound action.

nodes.title: Object-Level Authorization
nodes.summary: Authorize ownership, tenant, and action rights against the server-loaded object rather than trusting IDs, hidden fields, roles, or bulk selectors. This prevents IDOR and horizontal privilege escalation.
nodes.probe: Create equivalent objects for users or tenants A and B, replay A's read/update/delete/export/download requests with B identifiers and bulk arrays, and assert 403/404 with no partial side effect.

nodes.title: Function-Level Authorization
nodes.summary: Enforce explicit role and scope policies for privileged functions independently of client navigation or UI visibility. This prevents direct invocation of administrative, debug, export, impersonation, billing, and bulk actions.
nodes.probe: Execute a role-by-route negative matrix against admin, debug, export, impersonation, billing, and bulk endpoints with client controls bypassed; assert ordinary roles always receive 403 and create no side effect.

nodes.title: Least Privilege Scopes
nodes.summary: Grant users, services, databases, queues, cloud identities, and operators only the minimum scopes, roles, resources, and actions required. This limits exposure and destructive blast radius after compromise.
nodes.probe: Parse effective IAM, OAuth, database, and service-account policies for wildcard grants and compare them with an approved permission set. Fail on unowned, unexpired unexplained administrative access and verify a workload cannot read or mutate an unrelated resource.

nodes.title: SQL Injection Prevention
nodes.summary: Keep query code and values separate through parameter binding or safe ORM APIs, allowlist dynamic identifiers, validate inputs, and restrict database privileges. This prevents attacker input changing query structure or accessing unauthorized data.
nodes.probe: Send quote, comment, boolean, union, time-delay, and type-confusion payloads through every query input; assert no SQL error, row-set expansion, or timing oracle. Statically inspect query construction and parse database grants for excess privileges.

nodes.title: XSS Prevention
nodes.summary: Encode output for its actual context, sanitize explicitly permitted rich HTML, avoid unsafe DOM sinks, and use Trusted Types where supported. This prevents injected script stealing sessions, reading PII, or acting as the victim.
nodes.probe: Inject script tags, quote payloads, URL schemes, SVG, and event-handler strings into every rendered field; assert encoded/sanitized output and no script execution in a headless browser. Scan source and bundles for unreviewed unsafe sinks.

nodes.title: Command Injection Prevention
nodes.summary: Never turn user input into shell syntax or an uncontrolled executable path; constrain unavoidable process execution by executable, arguments, identity, filesystem, and resources. This prevents arbitrary OS commands and limits helper-process damage.
nodes.probe: Fuzz every process input with ;id, &&id, $(id), newlines, option-injection, NULs, and argument-boundary payloads; assert no child beyond the fixed executable and no shell expansion. Inspect process-spawn configuration for shell execution and privilege.

nodes.title: SSRF Egress Controls
nodes.summary: Allowlist outbound schemes, hosts, ports, and redirects, re-check resolved addresses at connection time, and enforce network egress policy. This prevents fetchers reaching metadata, private services, and internal control planes.
nodes.probe: Exercise every server-side fetcher with loopback, RFC1918, IPv6-local, link-local/metadata, DNS-rebinding, non-HTTP, and redirect-chain targets; assert application rejection and blocked network egress. Verify approved external hosts still work.

nodes.title: Path Traversal Prevention
nodes.summary: Map external file identifiers to server-owned paths and enforce the intended base directory after canonical resolution. This rejects traversal, absolute paths, NULs, encoded separators, and unsafe symlink escapes.
nodes.probe: Exercise file endpoints with ../, encoded and double-encoded separators, absolute paths, NUL bytes, mixed separators, and symlink fixtures; assert rejection and verify no file outside the configured root is read or written.

nodes.title: Vault KMS Secret Delivery
nodes.summary: Store production secrets in managed Vault or KMS and deliver them at runtime through workload identity and path-level policy, never embedding values in source, images, bundles, or manifests. This prevents repository, registry, CI, and client-bundle compromise from exposing credentials.
nodes.probe: Scan source, git history, manifests, images, and built bundles with an approved secret scanner. Parse deployment policy for runtime Vault/KMS references, workload identity, and absence of static credential values; inspect one deployed workload for secret access logs.

nodes.title: Secret Rotation Revocation
nodes.summary: Assign owners and lifetimes to credentials and keys, automate rotation and emergency revocation, and make predecessors unusable after cutover. This limits leaked-credential lifetime and provides a tested compromise response.
nodes.probe: Parse secret metadata for owner, maximum age, last rotation, and revocation capability. Run a staging rotation, assert the new credential works without source changes, the old credential fails after cutover, and dependent services recover.

nodes.title: Secret Leak Prevention
nodes.summary: Scan working trees, history, CI output, releases, images, support exports, and registries with push protection before publication. Detection must trigger revocation and replacement because deleting one copy cannot erase retained history or caches.
nodes.probe: Run a secret scanner against full repository history, CI artifacts, container layers, release bundles, and support exports. Inject a canary credential into a test change and assert publication is blocked and the canary is revoked after detection.

nodes.title: Log Redaction
nodes.summary: Remove or irreversibly transform sensitive fields before logs, traces, metrics, crash reports, or support exports, including credentials and unnecessary PII. This prevents observability systems from becoming credential and PII exfiltration channels.
nodes.probe: Send canary secrets, tokens, passwords, and PII through success and error paths; export logs, traces, metrics, crash reports, and support data; assert exact and decoded canary values are absent from every sink.

nodes.title: Dependency Vulnerability Gates
nodes.summary: Lock direct and transitive dependencies, run SCA and license policy checks, and block exploitable high or critical findings without a current owned exception. Deterministic resolution ensures the scanned set is the shipped set.
nodes.probe: Run each package manager's audit and approved SCA/license scanners against every lockfile, generated bundle, and release image. Assert reproducible resolution and fail on unexpired policy violations or missing exception owners.

nodes.title: Container Hardening Scanning
nodes.summary: Build minimal digest-pinned images that run with reduced privileges and scan image layers, IaC, and runtime configuration before deployment. This reduces known CVE exposure and limits damage from compromise or escape.
nodes.probe: Build the release image and inspect effective user, root filesystem, capabilities, seccomp, mounts, and base digest. Run approved image/IaC CVE scanners and parse deployment securityContext for violations; assert policy failures block deployment.

nodes.title: Release SBOM
nodes.summary: Generate and retain a complete SPDX or CycloneDX inventory for every immutable release, tied to its exact artifact digest and build identifier. This enables rapid impact analysis across direct, transitive, bundled, runtime, and container-layer components.
nodes.probe: Generate the SBOM in CI, parse it for every package and container layer, and assert the release digest and build ID match the immutable artifact. Verify a published artifact cannot be promoted without its corresponding SBOM.

nodes.title: Provenance Signing Verification
nodes.summary: Record build provenance in isolated CI, sign artifacts and SBOMs, and verify expected source, builder, digest, and policy at deployment. This rejects altered, unauthorized, unsigned, and locally rebuilt releases.
nodes.probe: Verify a release signature and provenance against expected repository, revision, builder identity, and digest. Submit unsigned, mismatched, expired, and locally rebuilt artifacts to deployment and assert each is rejected.

nodes.title: TLS Baseline
nodes.summary: Use authenticated TLS 1.2 or 1.3 with approved ciphers, disable legacy protocols and weak renegotiation, validate certificates, automate renewal, and use mTLS where warranted. This prevents downgrade, interception, weak-cryptography exposure, and expiry outages.
nodes.probe: Run openssl s_client or an approved TLS scanner against every public and internal listener; assert legacy protocols and weak suites fail, hostname/chain validation succeeds, expiry is above threshold, and renewal works in a staging fixture.

nodes.title: Content Security Policy
nodes.summary: Deploy restrictive CSP policies using nonces or hashes and explicit source allowlists, prohibiting unexplained unsafe directives. This limits XSS impact and exposes unsafe inline regressions through violation reporting.
nodes.probe: Parse response headers and assert approved script/style sources, nonce/hash use, no unexplained unsafe directives, and required frame/object restrictions. Run a browser injection fixture and assert execution is blocked and a violation report is recorded.

nodes.title: HSTS
nodes.summary: Send HSTS for at least one year and include subdomains only after confirming every subordinate host is HTTPS-safe. This prevents first-visit and downgrade exposure of cookies and PII.
nodes.probe: Run curl -sS -D - https://host/ and assert Strict-Transport-Security: max-age>=31536000 with the approved subdomain decision. Request HTTP and assert a redirect with no content or cookie issuance before HTTPS.

nodes.title: CORS Allowlist
nodes.summary: Allow only exact reviewed origins and required methods and headers, never wildcard origins with credentials, and vary caches by Origin. This prevents hostile origins reading authenticated responses and abusing broad trust.
nodes.probe: Send trusted, untrusted, null, wildcard-like, and credentialed origins to preflight and actual endpoints; assert CORS headers appear only for exact allowlist entries and never combine wildcard origin with credentials.

nodes.title: Abuse Rate Limiting
nodes.summary: Apply endpoint-specific quotas and adaptive throttles keyed by trusted account, tenant, device, token, and network signals to sensitive and expensive operations. This limits stuffing, brute force, scraping, exhaustion, and spoofable-IP bypasses.
nodes.probe: Send bursts exceeding login, recovery, read, write, and expensive-operation quotas from one and many keys; assert 429, valid Retry-After, audit events, and no bypass through spoofed headers. Verify progressive friction activates for credential stuffing while an approved low-volume user remains usable.

nodes.title: Security Audit Logging
nodes.summary: Maintain an immutable, access-controlled audit trail for security-relevant actions with actor, target, outcome, time, and correlation context, without credentials or unnecessary PII. This supplies evidence for abuse investigation and accountability.
nodes.probe: Inspect current audit playbook and implementation evidence: in staging trigger authentication, authorization, admin, export, secret, and configuration events; parse the sink schema for actor, target, outcome, time, and correlation ID; attempt mutation/deletion with a normal operator identity and verify append-only controls.

nodes.title: PII Encryption at Rest
nodes.summary: Classify and minimize PII, encrypt every persisted store and backup with KMS-managed envelope keys separated by environment and access role, and retain policy-controlled application access. This limits disclosure from disks, snapshots, exports, and broad decrypt permissions.
nodes.probe: Inspect storage, backup, queue, and cache configuration for KMS key IDs and environment separation; sample a persisted record or object and verify ciphertext at rest. Confirm an unauthorized service identity cannot decrypt and that a restore test succeeds.

nodes.title: PII in Transit and Minimization
nodes.summary: Require authenticated encrypted channels for every PII hop, exclude PII from URLs and telemetry, and apply documented purpose, retention, deletion, and minimization rules. This reduces network, logging, analytics, and retained-data exposure.
nodes.probe: Inspect transport, telemetry, and retention evidence: send a canary PII value through representative requests and telemetry; inspect URLs, proxy/access logs, traces, metrics, queues, and exports for plaintext; parse TLS configuration and retention/deletion jobs for each PII store.

nodes.title: Incident Response Readiness
nodes.summary: Maintain owner-assigned playbooks for credential compromise, data breach, dependency/CVE, and ransomware with containment, evidence preservation, eradication, recovery, notification, authority, and tested contacts. This reduces containment delay and missed obligations under pressure.
nodes.probe: Inspect current playbooks for token/credential, breach, CVE, and ransomware scenarios, verify named owners and notification paths, and review a recent tabletop or technical exercise with closed findings. Confirm evidence-preservation and revocation steps are executable in staging.
